input.quote: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs for an initial five (5) year term with automatic one-year renewals (§ 11.1) and the only exits are uncured material breach or insolvency (§ 11.2); no Corio convenience termination right exists anywhere in the document, and there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term fails both preferred and fallback, so we target the preferred level with a single new Section 11.3 (numbered inline so it matches the Section 11 scheme): Corio, as the customer, may terminate for convenience on 30 days' prior written notice, Commerce One refunds prepaid fees pro rata, and Commerce One has no convenience termination right during the initial or any renewal term. The § 11.1 mutual non-renewal notice is natural-term non-renewal (a RENEWAL matter effective at expiration), so it is not flagged here as a Vendor mid-term convenience right and is left verbatim.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 11.3 giving Corio, as the customer, convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and barring Commerce One from convenience termination during the term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11 commits us to a five-year term with exits only for breach or insolvency, so we have added a new Section 11.3 giving us a convenience termination right on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Commerce One has no convenience exit during the term. If you prefer, we can move to our fallback of 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.text: 11.3 Termination for Convenience. Corio, as the customer, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, pro rata, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.
